description:
MEGA Genesis es un equipo de jóvenes apasionados por la ciencia, la tecnología y la innovación. Inspirados por Generación MEGA, creemos en el poder de las metas con propósito, la creatividad y el trabajo en equipo. Participamos en el NASA Space Apps Challenge para transformar ideas en soluciones, superar desafíos y contribuir a un futuro mejor mediante la exploración espacial.

Beyond Limits. Driven by Purpose.
summary:
Space Mission is an educational game built with Phaser that puts players in charge of planning and testing a space mission. Players launch a rocket, experiment with its orbit, and make decisions about spacecraft, scientific instruments, and how to use limited resources on a mission to the Moon and back. The simulation evaluates these choices using predefined rules and explains how they affect the outcome.

The project addresses the challenge by turning space mission design into a hands-on experience. Its pixel-art style makes the game approachable, while its mechanics ask players to balance engineering constraints, scientific goals, and limited resources. Students can try different approaches and see why a choice that helps one part of the mission might make another harder.
details:
Space Mission is an educational browser game developed by MEGA Genesis for the NASA Space Apps Challenge. GitHub: https://github.com/cbrenesC/MEGA-Genesis/tree/main

Inspired by the Space Mission Design Game challenge, it puts players in a pixel-art mission control center where they can talk to crew members, use workstations, and make the engineering decisions behind a space mission.

The main mission takes players to the Moon and back. Players launch a rocket, experiment with its orbit, and see how their decisions affect the flight and return to Earth. The game also offers a separate lunar rover mission that players can try before completing the main mission. They choose components and scientific instruments, then test their design by exploring the Moon, collecting samples, and transmitting data.

The game teaches engineering through trade-offs. Adding an instrument can expand what a rover can study, but it can also increase its mass, power consumption, and cost. Players must weigh scientific goals against constraints such as budget, mass, power, communications, and launch capacity. Mathematical calculations and predefined game rules determine which designs meet the constraints and how the mission unfolds. AI supports the explanations that help players interpret those results.

We built Space Mission with Phaser and used AI tools to support development and create game assets. The visual style draws on Terraria’s pixel art and on spaceflight simulators. The game runs directly in a web browser without requiring installation. Our goal was to make space mission design something students can learn by doing. When a design falls short, they can change it, test it again, and see what difference their choices made.

As players progress, they can earn and collect 12 unique pixel-art medals by completing mission configuration tasks and simulations. Special gold medals reward successful missions, encouraging players to improve their designs, overcome challenges, and complete their collection. Once all medals are earned, players can download and share their achievement collection.
